newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends just 7 cts off on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends just 7 cts off on short-covering.

text.p: IPE September Brent climbed well above lows where it languished for most of Monday to last trade just seven cents down at $18.92 a barrel, brokers said.
"There was some short-covering towards the close but there is no real news out there," said one broker.

Fears that the summer rally in U.S. gasoline markets was about to end tipped Brent lower earlier in the day and most trade was in the $18.75-$18.85 range. Weak unleaded futures and WTI held London values down after New York markets opened.
But all contracts made up some lost ground just before the close, with September gasoline ending a cent above day lows.

The September unleaded bounced off its most significant recent support of 64.40 cents a gallon twice during the day and finished at 65.40. September WTI recovered from its $19.67 trough and ended down 13 cents at $19.94 a barrel.
"Gasoline was obviously what kept things moving during the day but over all we were very quiet," said one broker.
Reports that refiner Tosco's 130,000 barrel per day cat cracker was running again after a three-week maintenance shutdown had gasoline markets trembling.
Its absence has been a key prop to the soaring mogas market, which in turn had buoyed the rest of the oil complex.
Tosco itself was keeping mum on the health of its monster gasoline producing unit, the biggest in the world.

IPE gas oil had earlier last traded $2 lower and settled $1.75 off at $169.50 a tonne, just above support. Business was quiet with physical gas oil solid, but heavy paper selling at the end pushed values closer to the $169 target.
"Whenever we tried to rally on the gas oil we got knocked back down again," said one broker. "I think we were seeing some sellers getting signals from the computer programmes."
Despite the losses on the day most dealers looking at the pattern for the week ahead still saw support from gasoline.
Summer demand for motor fuel is still healthy and refinery margins are rosy, boosting crude markets that have for now shrugged off the effect of resumed Iraqi crude exports.
On the technical side a cluster of support levels in the range from $18.40 to $18.70 is giving IPE Brent a safety net.
"There has been a bit of pressure on the selling side which has given it a more bearish tone but the volumes are not there to make it dump," said one broker.
